Fingerprint a capture's column set

Source: R/crt_schema_fingerprint.R
crt_schema_fingerprint.Rd

Computes the schema_version value the nge/form_capture schema declares: <n>-<digest>, where n is the number of columns and digest is the 64-bit xxHash, in hex, of the columns' name:TYPE pairs sorted by name and joined with commas.

Usage

crt_schema_fingerprint(types)

Arguments

types

Named character vector of declared column types, one element per column, names being the column names.

Value

A string, <n>-<16 hex digits>.

Details

The rule lives here so that every producer computes it the same way. Two producers that differed would give two different vintages the same version, or one vintage two versions, and nothing downstream could tell.

What goes in

Pass the capture's own columns with the types the file declares, as a named character vector: c(date_time_start = "DATETIME", gravel = "REAL"). For a GeoPackage that is PRAGMA table_info()'s type. Leave out the geometry column and any surrogate row id the reader supplies rather than the capture carrying, such as a GeoPackage fid.

Types are part of the pair because a column that changes type between vintages is a real schema change, and a fingerprint of names alone would report it as none. They are upper-cased first, so real and REAL agree. Names are sorted in C collation, so the value does not depend on the machine's locale, and column order does not move it.

What gets hashed

The bytes of the joined string, not R's serialization of it. A hash of a serialized object depends on the serialization format, which R can change without any schema change behind it, and no other language could reproduce it. The digest is the standard XXH64 with seed 0, so any implementation of it gives the same value from the same string.

Examples

types <- c(date_time_start = "DATETIME", wetted_width_m = "REAL",
           crew_members = "TEXT")
crt_schema_fingerprint(types)
#> [1] "3-53a53c8bae8940fa"

# Column order does not matter; a changed type does.
crt_schema_fingerprint(rev(types))
#> [1] "3-53a53c8bae8940fa"
crt_schema_fingerprint(replace(types, "wetted_width_m", "TEXT"))
#> [1] "3-6240cab34f1c197c"
